doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: Comparing late-night bands today
summary: Henderson on today's late-night bands as vaudeville and loud.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: When you listen to — or I don’t know if you do — but when you hear the bands that are playing for the late night shows now—

I can’t stand it. I have to confess. I shouldn’t say that. They are doing what they should be doing. But you know they are in essence what we were, the vaudeville bands. We were a vaudeville band when The Prince, as we called Carson, or Steve Allen, when it wasn’t going, we had all kinds of schtick that we would do, we were like a traveling circus. That’s when Doc started doing his accent. I mean everything like that. We had bits that we would do to crank up the studio, you know, it was a fascinating time to watch so it was really vaudeville. And that’s what I feel these small combos are. They’re loud. That’s the only thing that bothers me is the huge volume that they put out.
Someone floored me once recently, they said whistle any of the theme songs from the late night shows these days.
